title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks sold off Friday (Oct 30) — Nasdaq -2.9%, S&P 500 -1.8%, Dow -1.1% — as Intel plunged 29% on weak Q4 guidance and a warning that PC sales are tanking; Reddit also fell 29% on growth worries.
Markets: Flight to bonds — the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.93%, its steepest monthly drop since Dec 2023; gold slid ~3.7% and Bitcoin fell ~5% to below $77K amid crypto-hack fallout.
Companies: Binance halted trading after hackers linked to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit stole $6.3B — the largest crypto heist ever; Coinbase shares dropped 12%.
Companies: Big Oil topped estimates on refining strength — Exxon $15.4B, Chevron $9.9B, BP $8.5B in Q3 profit — while Rivian jumped ~7% premarket on an earnings beat and strong R2 SUV demand.
Companies: DoorDash is pitching its $17B Instacart deal as a way to help small retailers compete with Amazon and Walmart; Amazon shares stay pressured after Thursday's AI-capex cash-flow warning.
Macro/Policy: Three Fed officials signaled support for a December rate hike even after this week's hold at 3.75%-4.00%, keeping markets on edge over the policy path.
Macro/Policy: Labor Dept. finalized a rule forcing pharmacy benefit managers (CVS Caremark, Express Scripts, Optum Rx) to disclose fees and spread pricing starting next July.
Macro/Policy: A bipartisan energy permitting bill is hitting Democratic resistance (Rep. Casten) over fears it favors a natural-gas buildout over renewables amid AI-driven power demand.
